decisions.reason: Report grounds the analysis in the fixture package.json (declaration ^0.1.2-alpha.1) and README, explicitly states alpha.1 was never published while alpha.2, 0.1.1-rc.1 and 0.1.1-rc.2 were, clearly labels the registry fact as supplied evidence rather than a live query, and proposes registry verification only as a future authorized step. It does not infer package existence from the root package or a dist-tag.

Explains that the missing alpha.1 lower bound does not make ^0.1.2-alpha.1 unresolvable: an offline semver computation normalizes it to >=0.1.2-alpha.1 <0.2.0-0 with default prerelease same-tuple eligibility, so 0.1.2-alpha.2 is selected. It identifies the silent declaration/type-baseline substitution, notes semver acceptance is not compatibility proof, and correctly rejects 0.1.1-rc.x and cross-tuple prereleases without claiming all alphas are missing.

Gives three complete plans with tradeoffs: (A) exact-pin the published 0.1.2-alpha.2 and update docs, explicitly acknowledging this does not validate alpha.1; (B) verify the upstream alpha.1 tag, build/pack the full required cohort and resolve local tarballs with scoped overrides; (C) a type-only verification lane. Each is concrete and internally coherent, going well beyond bare tarball/overrides keywords.

Commits to one package manager chosen from the real repo (explicitly refusing to introduce pnpm without cause), proposes a committed lockfile reproduced via npm ci/frozen equivalent, a typecheck against the intended target including declaration-owner checks, and exit paths: replacing local alpha.1 tarball overrides with verified published cohort versions while regenerating the lockfile, or deliberate future upgrades for the pin plan. Unverified source/build/runtime details are marked unconfirmed throughout.

caps.reason: No affirmative prescription to npm-install the unpublished alpha.1 cohort. Plan A pins the published alpha.2; Plan B obtains alpha.1 by building local tarballs from a verified source tag, which the cap excludes; rejected bad examples are quoted only to be rejected.
